Whernside.credit: Cyberdemon007 at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0
Whernside.about: The highest of the Yorkshire Three Peaks and of the Dales: a long ridge above the Ribblehead Viaduct on the Settle–Carlisle line.

routes.name: Ribblehead
routes.text: Past the viaduct and up beside the railway, then by Force Gill onto the ridge and south along it. The Three Peaks route.

routes.name: Chapel-le-Dale
routes.text: Steep and direct up the stone steps from Bruntscar.

routes.name: Dentdale
routes.text: From Dentdale, the Craven Way, an old packhorse track, climbs over the north-east shoulder; leave it for the ridge.

Ingleborough.about: A flat-topped gritstone fortress, ringed by the remains of an Iron Age hillfort wall, with a cross-shaped wind shelter and a trig point.

routes.name: Clapham via Gaping Gill
routes.text: Past Ingleborough Cave and through the limestone gorge of Trow Gill to the Gaping Gill pothole, then up Little Ingleborough.

routes.name: Ingleton via Crina Bottom
routes.text: Up Fell Lane and past Crina Bottom farm to the steep final climb. Fell Lane is a bridleway all the way to the summit.

routes.name: Chapel-le-Dale
routes.text: The Three Peaks route across Humphrey Bottom and up the stone staircase.

Great Shunner Fell.about: The third-highest fell in the Dales, a broad grassy hill between Wensleydale and Swaledale crossed by the Pennine Way.

routes.name: Hardraw on the Pennine Way
routes.text: From Hardraw near Hawes, the Pennine Way climbs the long, gentle south-east ridge. Easy to follow, flagged across the boggy parts.

routes.name: Thwaite on the Pennine Way
routes.text: From Thwaite in Swaledale, steadily up the north-east ridge.

High Seat.about: The highest point of Mallerstang Edge, the long gritstone escarpment above the head of the Eden valley.

routes.name: From Mallerstang
routes.text: The usual way, from the valley road (B6259) at Outhgill, steeply up the western flank onto the edge.

routes.name: Along Mallerstang Edge
routes.text: North from Hugh Seat and Lady Anne's Pillar, or south from the Kirkby Stephen–Keld road, along the rough, wet top of the edge.

Wild Boar Fell.credit: Matt westwood at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0
Wild Boar Fell.about: A flat-topped fell with a dramatic gritstone scarp above Mallerstang, where the last wild boar in England was said to have been killed.

routes.name: From Mallerstang via The Nab
routes.text: From the B6259, under the Settle–Carlisle railway and up to The Nab, the fell's northern prow, then along the edge.

routes.name: Ridge from Swarth Fell
routes.text: Along the grassy ridge from Swarth Fell to the south, often walked as a horseshoe from Aisgill.

Great Whernside.credit: StephenDawson at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 2.0
Great Whernside.about: A long gritstone ridge between Wharfedale and Nidderdale with a rocky summit crest; not to be confused with Whernside.

routes.name: Kettlewell via Hag Dyke
routes.text: Up past Hag Dyke, an old farmhouse that is now a scout hostel, and the steep edge to the summit rocks.

routes.name: Park Rash
routes.text: From the top of the steep Kettlewell–Coverdale road, south along the ridge.

Buckden Pike.about: A broad top above Upper Wharfedale with a memorial cross to five Polish airmen killed when their Wellington bomber crashed here in a blizzard in 1942.

routes.name: Buckden
routes.text: From the village car park, a path climbs steadily up the hillside to the summit ridge and the trig point by the wall.

routes.name: Starbotton
routes.text: Up the Walden Road bridleway from Starbotton to the ridge, then north past the memorial cross.

Pen-y-ghent.about: A lion-shaped hill above Horton in Ribblesdale, the smallest and most distinctive of the Three Peaks.

routes.name: Horton via Brackenbottom
routes.text: Up past Brackenbottom farm to the stepped nose of the hill and a short scramble up its rocky tiers.

routes.name: Horton via Hunt Pot
routes.text: The Pennine Way up Horton Scar Lane (a bridleway), then past the potholes of Hull Pot and Hunt Pot.

Great Coum.about: A quiet top above Dentdale. The County Stone just below it once marked where Yorkshire, Lancashire and Westmorland met.

routes.name: Dent via Flinter Gill
routes.text: Up the steep, stony lane of Flinter Gill to the Occupation Road (a bridleway well known to riders), then up beside the wall.

routes.name: White Shaw Moss
routes.text: The shortest way, from the minor road between Dent and Kingsdale.

Swarth Fell.about: A quiet fell on the ridge south of Wild Boar Fell, above the Settle–Carlisle railway's summit at Aisgill.

routes.name: Horseshoe from Aisgill
routes.text: From the B6259 near Aisgill, up onto the ridge and over both Swarth Fell and Wild Boar Fell.

routes.name: Ridge from Wild Boar Fell
routes.text: South along the grassy ridge past a line of tarns.
